import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/training_2.csv"

# Step 1: Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
df_source2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']

# Step 2: Join the source tables to form the target schema
# Target schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float]

# Join df_source1 and df_source2 on 'movie_id' to get title with ratings and timestamps
df_join_1_2 = pd.merge(df_source1, df_source2[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Join the above result with df_source0 on 'user_id' to get age and occupation
df_full = pd.merge(df_join_1_2, df_source0[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Step 3: Convert columns to target data types and order columns as per target schema
# 'title': string
df_full['title'] = df_full['title'].astype(str)

# 'user_id': float
df_full['user_id'] = df_full['user_id'].astype(float)

# 'movie_id': integer
df_full['movie_id'] = df_full['movie_id'].astype(int)

# 'rating': float
df_full['rating'] = df_full['rating'].astype(float)

# 'timestamp': float
df_full['timestamp'] = df_full['timestamp'].astype(float)

# 'age': float
df_full['age'] = df_full['age'].astype(float)

# 'occupation': float
df_full['occupation'] = df_full['occupation'].astype(float)

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema exactly
df_target = df_full[['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']]

# Step 4: Save the transformed dataframe to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 and Source2 on movie_id
join_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source0 on user_id
joined = pd.merge(join_1_2, source0, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost columns of the target schema that are not float:
# title (string), user_id (float but used as group key), movie_id (int), rating (float but used as group key), timestamp (float but used as group key)
# According to hints, group by title, user_id, movie_id, rating, timestamp
# Aggregate age and occupation by mean (float columns not in group by)
grouped = joined.groupby(
    ["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp"], as_index=False
).agg(
    age=("age", "mean"),
    occupation=("occupation", "mean")
)

# Write output with exact target schema column order
grouped = grouped[["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "age", "occupation"]]

grouped.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_25/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
